words.ex: I love fruit, especially strawberries.
use: The hotel is busy, especially on weekends.
mcq: I like summer, specially August season.
Especially, I like the August most.
words.note: especially는 예시 앞에 붙어요. specially(특별히 맞춤으로)와 구분!

words.ex: We went out despite the rain.
use: Despite the price, the room was small.
mcq: Despite of the rain, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out.
Despite it rained, we went out.
Despite for the rain, we went out.
words.note: despite + 명사 바로 연결! 'despite of'는 정말 흔한 오류예요(in spite of와 혼동).

words.ex: The buffet has a variety of dishes.
use: We offer a variety of room types.
I eat a variety of vegetables.
mcq: They sell a variety of drinks.
words.note: a variety of + 복수명사. 관사 a를 빼먹기 쉬워요!

words.ex: I'm preparing for a job interview.
use: She prepared dinner for the guests.
We need to prepare for the busy season.
words.note: prepare for + 대비할 일. prepare + 명사(직접 만들 것)도 가능해요.

words.ex: Only two rooms remain available.
words.note: remain + 형용사 = ~한 상태로 있다. 부사가 아니라 형용사!

words.ex: Can you describe the problem?
use: She described the room in detail.
words.note: describe + 대상 바로 연결! describe about은 대표적인 한국식 오류.

words.ex: She manages a small hotel.
use: I managed to finish on time.
He manages a team of ten people.
mcq: I managed to catch the bus.
I managed for catching the bus.
words.note: manage to + 동사 = (힘들었지만) 해내다. -ing가 아니에요!

words.ex: Pets are not allowed in this hotel.
words.exko: 이 호텔은 반려동물 출입이 안 돼요.
use: My parents allowed me to travel alone.
words.note: allow + 사람 + to부정사. 수동태 be allowed to도 자주 써요.

words.ex: I decided to learn English.
use: Have you decided what to order?
mcq: I decided to change my job.
words.note: decide + to부정사. decide -ing는 안 돼요!

words.ex: Let me explain the check-in process.
use: Can you explain it again slowly?
She explained the rules to the guests.
mcq: Please explain the rule to me.
Please explain to me it the rule.
words.note: explain A to B! 'explain me'는 안 돼요 — 꼭 to가 필요해요.

words.ex: Did you notice anything strange?
use: I noticed a small stain on the sheet.
시트에 작은 얼룩이 있는 걸 발견했다.
mcq: I noticed that he was tired.
I noticed about he was tired.
words.note: notice + that절 / notice + 명사. notice about은 어색해요.

words.ex: Are you ready to order?
use: I ordered room service last night.
The names are in alphabetical order.
mcq: I ordered a pasta and a salad.
words.note: order + 음식 바로 연결. 식당·호텔에서 매일 쓰는 동사예요!

words.ex: Breakfast is served from 7 to 10.
mcq: Dinner is serving at 6 by us.
words.note: be served = 제공되다. 호텔·식당 영어의 핵심 동사!

words.ex: Let me share my screen.
use: We shared a room during the trip.
mcq: Can you share the file with me?
Can you share me the file?
Can you share the file to I?
Can you share for me the file?
words.note: share A with B. 'share me'는 안 돼요!

words.ex: Thank you for your support.
words.note: support + 대상 바로 연결. be동사 넣지 않기!

words.ex: They offered me the job!
mcq: She offered to drive me home.
words.note: offer + to부정사 = ~해 주겠다고 하다.

words.ex: Did you receive my email?
use: I received a gift from a guest.
words.note: '잘 받았습니다'는 I received it (well은 문장 끝에, 또는 생략이 더 자연스러워요).

words.ex: Your English is improving fast!
use: I want to improve my service skills.
words.note: improve 하나로 충분! improve up 같은 군더더기는 필요 없어요.

words.ex: It depends on the weather.
use: The price depends on the season.
mcq: It is depend on your choice.
words.note: depend on! of/to가 아니고, be동사도 넣지 않아요.

words.ex: Let me introduce myself.
use: She introduced me to her manager.
The hotel introduced a new service.
mcq: Let me introduce my friend to you.
Let me introduce you my friend.
Let me introduce my friend for you.
Let me introduce to my friend you.
words.note: introduce A to B = A를 B에게 소개하다. 순서와 to가 핵심!

words.ex: I didn't expect to see you here!
use: We expect the package to arrive tomorrow.
Don't expect too much from the movie.
mcq: I expect that he will come.
He expects me that I go.
words.note: expect + that절 / expect + to부정사. 'expect him coming'은 어색해요.

words.ex: Can I suggest a different plan?
use: I suggest that we take a break.
mcq: I suggest you to go home early.
I suggest to go home early.
words.note: suggest + -ing! 'suggest to go'는 한국인이 가장 많이 틀리는 형태예요.

words.ex: I totally agree with you.
use: We agreed to meet next week.
I don't agree with that idea.
words.note: agree with + 사람/의견. 'I am agree'는 be동사 없이 I agree!

words.ex: What time does the train arrive?
use: We arrived at the hotel around noon.
She arrived in Seoul last night.
words.note: arrive at + 장소(건물), arrive in + 도시/나라. arrive to는 없어요!

words.ex: Will you attend the meeting tomorrow?
use: About fifty people attended the seminar.
I can't attend the wedding this Saturday.
mcq: I will attend to the meeting.
I will attend at the meeting.
I will attend in the meeting.
words.note: attend + 행사 바로 연결! 전치사를 넣는 게 대표적인 실수예요.

words.ex: You can achieve anything if you try.
use: We achieved our sales goal this month.
She achieved great success in her career.
mcq: He achieved to pass the exam.
He achieved his goal at last.
words.note: achieve + 명사(목표·성공). achieve to는 쓰지 않아요.

words.ex: Please raise your hand if you have a question.
use: Can I raise one more question?
mcq: They raised the price last month.
The price was raise by them.
They rose the price last month.
words.note: raise는 목적어가 필요(올리다). 스스로 오르는 건 rise! rise-rose-risen과 혼동 주의.

words.ex: We finally reached the top of the mountain.
use: You can reach me by email anytime.
mcq: We reached to the station at 9.
We reached at the station at 9.
We reached in the station at 9.
words.note: reach + 장소 바로 연결! arrive at과 헷갈려서 reach to로 쓰기 쉬워요.

words.ex: She has a successful career in marketing.
words.exko: 그녀는 마케팅 분야에서 성공적인 커리어를 쌓았어요.
use: I want to change my career path.
He spent his whole career at one company.
mcq: I built my career in education.
words.note: career는 '직업명'이 아니라 '경력의 흐름'이에요. My job is~ 와 구분!

words.ex: My goal is to speak English fluently.
words.exko: 제 목표는 영어를 유창하게 하는 거예요.
use: We set a goal for this year.
mcq: I made a goal to exercise daily.
I set a goal to exercise daily.
I built a goal to exercise.
I put a goal to exercise.
words.note: 목표를 '세우다'는 set a goal! make보다 set이 자연스러워요.

words.ex: I'm having trouble with my computer.
use: He got into trouble at school.
mcq: I have trouble to sleep at night.
I have trouble sleeping at night.
I have a trouble for sleeping.
words.note: have trouble + -ing! 'trouble to sleep'이 아니에요.

words.ex: Please contact me if you have questions.
use: I'll contact you as soon as possible.
words.note: contact + 사람 바로 연결! contact to/with는 대표적인 한국식 오류예요.

words.ex: This watch has great sentimental value.
use: The value of the house went up.
mcq: This experience is value to me.
This experience has value to me.
words.note: have value = 가치가 있다. valuable(형용사)과 구분하세요.

words.ex: This is my second attempt at the test.
use: He attempted to fix it himself.
mcq: I attempted that I solve it.
words.note: attempt + to부정사. try보다 격식 있는 말이에요.

words.ex: Please let me know in advance.
use: Technology advances so fast these days.
Thank you in advance for your help.
words.note: in advance = 미리. 전치사 in이 고정이에요.

words.ex: The company has about 200 employees.
mcq: I am an employee at a bank.
I am an employer at a bank as staff.
I work as an employer for my boss.
words.note: employee = 고용된 직원, employer = 고용주(회사). -ee가 '받는 쪽'!

words.ex: I try to exercise three times a week.
words.note: do exercise 또는 그냥 exercise(동사). play는 구기 종목에만!

words.ex: Push the door, don't pull it.
use: Don't push me, I need time.
She pushed herself to finish the race.
mcq: He pushed me to try again.
He pushed that I try again.
He pushed to me for trying.
words.note: push + 사람 + to부정사 = ~하도록 밀어붙이다.

words.ex: The hotel provides free breakfast.
use: We provide customers with fast service.
The company provided lunch for everyone.
mcq: They provide us with good service.
They provide to us good service.
They provide good service for we.
words.note: provide A with B = A에게 B를 제공하다. with를 빼먹기 쉬워요!

words.ex: I just realized I left my phone at home.
words.exko: 폰을 집에 두고 온 걸 방금 깨달았어요.
use: She realized her mistake too late.
He finally realized his dream of opening a cafe.
그는 마침내 카페 여는 꿈을 이뤘다.
mcq: I realized that I was wrong.
I realized about I was wrong.
words.note: realize + that절. '실감하다'와 '꿈을 실현하다' 두 뜻 모두!

words.ex: I believe you can do it.
use: I can't believe it's already September!
mcq: I believe that he is honest.
I believe to he is honest.
I believe in that his honest.
words.note: believe + that절. believe in + 대상 = ~의 가치/존재를 믿다.

words.ex: Prices increased again this month.
use: 스트레스는 건강 위험을 높일 수 있다.
words.note: increase by + 수치 = ~만큼 증가. 반대말 decrease도 세트로!

words.ex: What's your plan for the weekend?
mcq: I'm planning to buy a new phone.
I'm planning buying a new phone.
I'm planning buy a new phone.
I plan that buying new phone.
words.note: plan to + 동사. according to plan(계획대로)도 유용!

words.ex: The test results come out Friday.
use: As a result, the meeting was canceled.
mcq: As a result, we changed the plan.
As the result of, we changed plan.
Resulting as, we changed the plan.
As result, we changed the plan it.
words.note: as a result = 그 결과. 문장 연결의 필수 표현!

words.ex: What happened to your phone?
mcq: What was happened to your car?
What did happened to your car?
words.note: happen to + 대상. 수동태 없이! was happened는 안 돼요.

words.ex: Now I understand what you mean.
use: Sorry, I don't understand this part.
죄송한데 이 부분이 이해가 안 돼요.
mcq: I am understanding your point now well.
words.note: understand는 진행형(-ing)으로 잘 안 써요! I understand로 충분.

words.ex: Don't spend too much on clothes.
use: I spent two hours cleaning the house.
We spent the holiday at home.
mcq: I spent an hour reading the report.
I spent an hour to read the report.
I spent an hour for read report.
An hour spent me reading report.
words.note: spend + 시간 + -ing! 'spend to read'가 최다 오류예요.

words.ex: I'm learning English with Brian!
use: She learned to drive last year.
mcq: I'm learning to cook Italian food.
Italian food learns me to cook.
words.note: learn to + 동사. study(공부하다)와 달리 '할 줄 알게 되다'!

words.ex: I hope you feel better soon.
use: We hope to see you again.
mcq: I hope that you pass the test.
I hope you to pass the test.
You hope me that pass test.
words.note: hope + that절 / hope to + 동사. hope 사람 to는 안 돼요(wish와 다름)!

words.ex: What's the reason for the delay?
use: The main reason is the cost.
mcq: The reason for the change is simple.
The reason of the change is simple.
The reason to change is simply.
Simple is the reason changing for.
words.note: reason for + 명사. reason of는 어색해요!

words.ex: How much does it cost?
words.note: cost + 금액 바로 연결. cost-cost-cost 무변화 동사!

words.ex: I wasn't able to sleep last night.
use: Will you be able to come?
She's able to speak three languages.
mcq: I'll be able to help you tomorrow.
I'll able to help you tomorrow.
I'll be able helping you tomorrow.
I be able to help tomorrow you.
words.note: be able to — be동사 빼먹지 않기! can의 미래·완료형 대타.

words.ex: Are you sure about that?
use: I'm not sure what to choose.
Make sure to lock the door.
mcq: Make sure to bring your ID.
Sure make to bring your ID.
words.note: make sure to + 동사 = 꼭 ~하세요. 당부의 필수 표현!

words.ex: Could you speak more slowly?
use: May I speak to Mr. Kim?
mcq: Can I speak to the manager?
Can I speak at the manager?
Can the manager speak me to?
words.note: speak to + 사람. 전화 영어의 첫 문장!

words.ex: Learning is a slow process.
use: The visa process takes two weeks.
We're in the process of moving.
mcq: We're in the process of hiring.
We're in the process to hiring.
The process is in we of hiring.
words.note: in the process of + -ing = ~하는 중. 격식 있는 '진행 중' 표현!

words.ex: She leads a team of five.
use: This road leads to the station.
mcq: Small habits lead to big changes.
Small habits lead for big changes.
Big changes lead small habits to.
words.note: lead to + 결과 = ~로 이어지다. lead-led-led!

words.ex: They're building a new mall nearby.
use: It takes time to build trust.
He built his business from nothing.
mcq: We're building a good habit together.
We're building up a good habit together grow.
We build a good habit be together.
A good habit builds we together.
words.note: build trust/habit/career — 물건만이 아니라 추상적인 것도 '쌓다'!

words.ex: Can you hold my bag for a second?
use: The meeting will be held on Friday.
mcq: The event will be held next month.
The event will be hold next month.
The event will hold next month itself.
Next month holds the event will.
words.note: be held = 열리다(행사). hold the line(전화 대기)도 실전 표현!

words.ex: I'll pay for lunch today.
mcq: I paid the coffee for her money.
words.note: pay for + 물건. pay off(결실을 맺다)는 보너스 표현!

words.ex: This is a present for you.
use: Everyone was present at the meeting.
She presented her idea to the team.
mcq: He presented the plan to the boss.
He presented the plan at the boss.
He presented to the plan the boss.
The plan presented him to boss.
words.note: present A to B = 발표하다. 선물·현재·발표, 삼형제 뜻!
